Definition: from G3089; something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price (figuratively, atonement):--ransom.
BiblicalUsage: The word names a ransom, the price paid to set someone free, and Jesus uses it for His own life: the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give His life a ransom for many. Matthew and Mark both keep the saying, and it stands at the heart of the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that ransom is the word that makes the cross personal: Jesus did not pay a price in the abstract, He gave His life for many, and I am one of them.
